papers.title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
papers.abstract: We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes. We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.

papers.title: Radiation Conditions and Uniqueness Theorems for Open Wave-guide Networks
papers.abstract: We state radiation conditions and prove a variety of uniqueness theorem for models of wave-guide networks, including acoustic wave-guide networks, and electromagnetic wave-guide networks described by the time harmonic Maxwell equations. To analyze Maxwell wave-guide networks we need to establish generalizations of the Mourre estimates from [29, 32].

papers.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
papers.abstract: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.

papers.title: Strict unimodality of the exact time-domain diffuse-light response under a Robin boundary condition
papers.abstract: Time-domain boundary measurements of diffuse light are temporal point-spread functions whose peak position is used as a robust scalar datum in diffuse optical and fluorescence imaging. We consider the exact response generated by a single fluorescent point target in a homogeneous half-space with a Robin boundary condition. The response is a temporal convolution of two diffusion Green-function factors containing a complementary-error-function boundary correction. For every positive diffusion, absorption, depth, and source--target and detector--target distance parameter, and for every nonnegative Robin parameter, we prove that the normalized exact response is a generalized gamma convolution density. Its extension by zero to the negative half-line is bell-shaped. A differentiable small-time expansion, established by sectorial analyticity and Cauchy estimates, together with the sign-change structure of the first two derivatives, excludes tangential critical points and yields a unique peak with strict increase before it and strict decrease after it. The argument is exact and requires no large-distance, source--detector balance, symmetry, restricted-time, or small-parameter assumption. The same conclusion holds after convolution with an exponential fluorescence-lifetime density for every positive lifetime. The key ingredients are an explicit Stieltjes representation of the Robin factor, hyperbolic complete monotonicity, closure of the generalized gamma convolution class, and bell-shape theory. A derivation of the exact half-space model and the differentiated endpoint asymptotics are included in two appendices.

papers.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.

papers.title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
papers.abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(\pi\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the Brillouin torus. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schr\"odinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

papers.title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
papers.abstract: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mari\~no and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.

papers.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
papers.abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

papers.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
papers.abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).

papers.title: Nonpersistence of full-dimensional tori with polynomial decay in nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract: We establish local nonpersistence of full-dimensional invariant tori with polynomially decaying actions for the periodic quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ iu_t-u_{xx}+T_vu+\mu|u|^4u=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb T:=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z). \] For every $\kappa\geq1$, we construct a fixed bounded real Fourier multiplier $T_ve^{ijx}=v_je^{ijx}$ whose frequencies $\lambda_j=j^2+v_j$ satisfy the Bourgain-type Diophantine condition \[ \operatorname{dist}\left(\sum_j\ell_j\lambda_j,\mathbb Z\right) \geq\gamma_\kappa\prod_j(1+\ell_j^2\langle j\rangle^{2\kappa})^{-1} \] for some $\gamma_\kappa>0$ and every nonzero finitely supported integer sequence $\ell$, where $\langle j\rangle=\max\{1,|j|\}$. For this multiplier, every $3<M<4\kappa+\frac12$, every $A>0$, and all sufficiently small $\mu A^2>0$, the closed relative action tube of radius $3/10$ around $I_j=A\langle j\rangle^{-M}$ contains no full-dimensional invariant torus in $H^1(\mathbb T)$ carrying a complete flow, with arbitrary frequencies allowed. This advances the study of the polynomial-decay problem identified by Kuksin as a main open problem in KAM theory for one-dimensional Hamiltonian PDEs [Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. Ser. 2, 212 (2004), 237--258, Problem 7.1]. Bourgain discussed a related question for short-range Hamiltonian systems [Russian Math. Surveys 59 (2004), 231--246, Section 3]. The proof combines simultaneous Diophantine and weighted homological estimates, an exact common-phase transformation, and one normal-form step on four adjacent Fourier coordinates. Uniform phase rotation forces an action excursion, while overlapping parameter intervals cover all sufficiently small positive perturbations. The mechanism suggests applications to other Hamiltonian PDEs.

papers.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
papers.abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

papers.title: A GLSM realization of derived equivalence in $U(1) \times U(2)$ models
papers.abstract: This paper studies the derived equivalence between Calabi--Yau mixed branches using the B-brane hemisphere partition function in anomalous gauged linear sigma models (GLSMs). For a family of anomalous $U(2)$ GLSMs, we study the infrared behavior of B-branes under RG flow and the variation of FI parameters in the quantum K\"ahler moduli space. As characterized by the big and small window categories of the GLSM, the RG flow effect is analyzed according to the properties of their B-brane central charges as hemisphere partition functions. The result generalizes the band restriction rules in anomalous abelian GLSMs (Clingempeel--Floch--Romo) to some $U(2)$ models. As an application, we study a family of $U(1)\times U(k)$ models for $k=1,2$, which realize a Fano UV sigma model and two IR phases as mixed branches accompanied by local Calabi--Yau Higgs components. By applying the restriction rules, we establish new derived equivalences between Calabi--Yau varieties from these anomalous models.

papers.title: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
papers.abstract: We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential $\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with insertion $\gamma_L=H^{L-1}/(L-1)!$, by its gravitational descendants, and by $\zeta(3)$ boundary terms coming from the Gamma class. At both loop orders the coefficient of $R^{L-1}$ in the Frobenius expansion in the mirror coordinate $R$ is $-\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with the Novikov variable $Q=\exp(R)$. At three loops the whole Feynman integral is an explicit expression in $\mathcal F_{\gamma_3}$ alone, because genus-zero recursion determines all descendant series from it; at four loops two diagonal series suffice, and the $\zeta(3)$ term is itself corrected by $\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_4}$. At three loops we also derive the analytic normalization independently, from the Picard--Fuchs equation and the polar part of a Mellin transform, prove integrality of the multiple-cover transforms for arbitrary integral insertions together with an explicit quantum-$K$ formula, and compute the exact period connection polynomials. Finally we give endpoint values along the Euclidean axis, bounds on the Taylor radii in the Novikov variable $Q$, a computer-assisted proof of the four-loop endpoint nonanalyticity, and a comparison of the normalizations at two, three and four loops.

papers.title: Degree Growth of Rational Maps with Laurent Property
papers.abstract: Algebraic entropy measures the exponential growth of the degrees of iterates of rational self-maps. It is introduced by Bellon and Viallet in \cite{BellonandViallet}. We study degree growth for rational maps arising from recurrences with the Laurent property, with particular emphasis on Gale--Robinson recurrences. We develop a direct method for determining the degree growth from the recurrence relation itself, reducing the problem to the study of associated max-linear, or tropical recurrences. We first obtain a closed formula for the degrees of iterates for a broad class of homogeneous quadratic Laurent recurrences. We then apply this result to the two-term Gale--Robinson family and derive an explicit quadratic growth formula with a periodic correction term. For three-term Gale--Robinson recurrences, we express the algebraic entropy in terms of the associated tropical growth rate sequence. Based on explicit computations, we formulate a conjecture for the general three-term family predicting quadratic growth with a periodic correction. We prove the conjecture for the infinite family with parameters $p=1$, $q=2$, and $r\geq3$.

papers.title: The \textsc{ABC}-equation revisited: missed integrable cases. Part I: classification and (quasi) integrable structures
papers.abstract: We consider the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$, which was proved to be integrable in the case $A + B + C = 0$ (the Veronese web equation). Our study reveals ten more cases that admit integrable structures that, to the best of our knowledge, where not known before. The techniques is based essentially on the theory of the tangent and cotangent coverings.

papers.title: Free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that translation-invariant free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance. Our proof is analytic in nature and it uses the bulk-edge correspondence. The central argument, which holds beyond the translation-invariant situation, is that in frustration-free models, edge modes cannot merge into the ground state band. We give an example of a gapped frustration-free model that is nonetheless gapless on the half-plane.

papers.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[ \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.

papers.title: A quadratic ancestor inequality for spanning trees
papers.abstract: We introduce a quadratic ancestor inequality for weighted spanning trees on finite undirected graphs and give two applications. First, for every finite $n$-vertex transitive graph, the expected distance in its uniform spanning tree (UST) between two independent uniform vertices is at least $\sqrt{n}-1$, resolving a conjecture in [Benjamini--Kozma, Comm. Math. Phys. 259 (2005), 257--286]. Second, we prove that the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) is at least 3/2.

papers.title: Computing the center of a fusion category
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm for explicitly computing the categorical (Drinfeld) center of a pivotal fusion category. Our approach is based on decomposing the images of simple objects under the induction functor from the category to its center. We have implemented this algorithm in a general-purpose software framework TensorCategories for tensor categories that we develop within the open-source computer algebra system OSCAR. We compute explicit models for the centers in form of the tuples $(X,\gamma)$ where $X$ is an object and $\gamma$ is a half-braiding. From these models we can compute the $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols. Using the data from the AnyonWiki, we were able to compute the center together with its $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols for all the 279 multiplicity-free fusion categories up to rank 5, and furthermore some chosen examples of rank 6, including the Haagerup subfactor (presented in a separate paper). Some of these centers yield new high-rank and not multiplicity-free examples of modular categories, e.g. rank 21 and multiplicity 2.

papers.title: Minimum nonlinearity for pattern-forming Turing instability in a mathematical autocatalytic model
papers.abstract: Pattern formation is ubiquitous in nature and the mechanism widely-accepted to underlay them is based on the Turing instability, predicted by Alan Turing decades ago. This is a non-trivial mechanism that involves nonlinear interaction terms between the different species involved and transport mechanisms. We present here a mathematical analysis aiming to explore the mathematical constraints that a reaction-diffusion dynamical model should comply in order to exhibit a Turing instability. The main conclusion limits the existence of this instability to nonlinearity degrees larger or equal to three.

papers.title: Arbitrarily Fast Quantum Dispersion in Long-Range Crystals
papers.abstract: We construct the first examples of one-dimensional long-range crystals exhibiting arbitrarily fast polynomial dispersive bounds. The Floquet functions of our Hamiltonians are highly oscillatory Weierstrass functions, whose rough autosimilar structure drives the fast dispersion. The proof develops a new Fourier decay theory for $C^\alpha$ images of the Lebesgue measure, based on a Dolgopyat-inspired transfer operator method, and yields a van der Corput lemma for Weierstrass functions. As a consequence, the local time of classical Weierstrass functions of sufficiently large lacunarity exists and is $C^k$, answering a question raised by Geman and Horowitz in 1980.

papers.title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
papers.abstract: It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed). The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the lifting a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states to a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere in the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.

papers.title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
papers.abstract: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(\rho_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(\rho_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.

papers.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove Poisson local eigenvalue statistics for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with nondegenerate Bernoulli potentials at any fixed nonzero coupling. After unfolding by the integrated density of states (IDS), the local eigenvalue process converges to a Poisson point process of unit intensity at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. The theorem also holds for bounded nonconstant iid potentials, provided the IDS is continuous and strictly increasing near the reference energy. If the IDS also has a finite positive derivative at that energy, the usual linear normalization gives the same limit. The proof uses a phase coordinate with exact IDS drift to obtain a uniform exponential crossing law and joint Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows.

papers.title: Approach to Equilibrium in Translation-Invariant Quantum Systems: Structural Results II
papers.abstract: We continue the development, started in [AHP 25 (2023), 715-749], of a structural theory of approach to equilibrium in translation-invariant quantum spin systems. Dynamical Steady States (DSS) are defined as w*-limit points of the time-averaged evolution of an initial state. We show that if a DSS is an equilibrium state of a sufficiently regular interaction, then the specific energy of this interaction is necessarily a constant of the motion. Two distinct mechanisms lead to this conclusion, one based on dynamical surface energies and the other on conservation of specific relative entropy. We conjecture that these properties hold for a natural class of interactions. For a DSS admitting a physical equilibrium description, the associated equilibrium states are characterized by a dynamical Gibbs variational principle: they are precisely the minimizers of the specific relative entropy from the initial state over the physical equilibrium states. The achieved minimum equals the increase of specific entropy. The structural theory also yields characterizations of approach to thermal equilibrium, based on two model-dependent questions: restoration of a sufficiently local thermodynamic description at large times and classification of the corresponding local constants of motion. Once locality is restored, the constants of motion determine the possible asymptotic equilibrium states. In particular, if finite-range locality is restored and the energy is the only finite-range constant of the motion, then every DSS is a thermal equilibrium state at the temperature fixed by energy conservation. The finite-time dynamical input underlying this theory is established in a companion paper.

papers.title: Dynamical Conservation Laws in Quantum Spin Systems
papers.abstract: We study dynamical conservation laws and the propagation of thermodynamic structure in translation-invariant lattice quantum spin systems. Using Lieb-Robinson bounds [CMP 28 (1972), 251-257] in arbitrary dimension, and Araki's bounds [CMP 14 (1969), 120-157] in dimension one, we prove conservation of the specific entropy, specific energy, and specific relative entropy under suitable assumptions on the interactions. The transported local Hamiltonians admit surface energies that vanish per unit volume in the van Hove limit, and local observables remain a core for the transported generators at every finite time. Weak Gibbsianity is preserved for sufficiently small times in arbitrary dimension and for all times in dimension one. These results provide the analytical foundation for the structural theory of approach to equilibrium developed in a companion paper, and establish partial results toward the conjectures formulated there.

papers.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
papers.abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which allows us to derive several new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is either $1$-Frobenius or Burnside.

papers.title: Fixed-Point Abundances and the Onset of Extinctions in Multispecies Lotka-Volterra Ecosystems
papers.abstract: I investigate the average and variance of species abundance distributions for fixed-point solutions to generalized Lotka-Volterra ecosystems. Two different analytical methods are constructed. First, I build up on the perturbative Random Matrix Theory approach developed in my earlier work [Phys. Rev. E. 113, L062202 (2026)], and formalize this method diagrammatically. The abundance average is given by a sum of planar diagrams with non-crossing vertex pairings which can be encoded as Dyck paths. This allows me to express the combinatorial factor multiplying perturbative terms at each order as Catalan and Narayana numbers, following which the abundance average is given by the latter's generating functions. In this way, the infinite perturbation expansion is exactly resummed in a closed-form formula. I have not been able to find a similar resummation for the abundance variance, however diagrammatic Feynman rules are expressed, following which the perturbative series can be calculated to any desirable order. Second, I do the same calculations using the cavity method, which gives closed-form formulas for both the abundance average and variance. For the average, the cavity formula gives the exact same result as the perturbative approach when the average interspecies interaction vanishes. When this is not the case, the two results are functionally different, however they are hardly distinguishable in their parametric range of validity. Comparison with numerical data indicate that the cavity result is more accurate over a larger parameter range.

papers.title: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
papers.abstract: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds are commonly called rigorous, yet as published they are not theorems: they hold at sampled points rather than on regions of parameter space, for truncated rational approximations of the conformal blocks, for a finite list of spins, and up to floating-point rounding. We close all four gaps. We show how to search efficiently for functionals positive on regions, including external-dimension space; how positivity on the large-spin crossing vectors can be imposed as such a region constraint; how new analytic bounds on the conformal-block recursion relations give functionals positive on the true, untruncated crossing vectors; and how to certify the positivity of these functionals in exact arithmetic. The certification rests on Bernstein-basis positivity certificates in up to three variables, exact arithmetic in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, a compactified treatment of the infinite spin tail, and an explicit bound on the difference between the true blocks and their truncations, so that infinitely many positivity conditions reduce to finitely many machine-checked sign conditions. As a flagship application we certify an exclusion region in the $(\Delta_\sigma,\Delta_\epsilon)$ plane: for $\Delta_\sigma\in[0.505,0.5405]$ all of $\Delta_\epsilon\in(1/2,3]$ is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, giving rigorous two-sided bounds on the critical exponents $\eta$ and $\nu$ under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. The analytic inputs for the mixed $\sigma$-$\epsilon$ system, which would remove the spin-2 gap assumption, are also proved. The same methods prevent common practical failure modes and can make bootstrap searches faster: region bounds turn the mapping of an island into a handful of one-dimensional bisections. The essential code to reproduce the search and the certification, and all machine-checkable certificates, are released.

papers.title: Infinite magic and the emergence of the continuum
papers.abstract: Which features of a quantum state are needed for a relativistic quantum field theory to emerge from a lattice system? We address this question by establishing a quantitative relationship between the type classification of hyperfinite von Neumann algebras and the quantum-information-theoretic resource of nonstabilizerness, also called magic. Our results establish two complementary parts of this relationship. First, we prove that any stabilizer system on a lattice defines a canonical GNS Hilbert space in which local von Neumann algebras do not contain type III factors in their central decomposition. As an explicit example, we prove that for stabilizer systems with short-range order, the local algebras are isomorphic to tensor products of hyperfinite factors of type I or type II. This demonstrates that the absence of magic is accompanied by the absence of type III factors in the local algebras, therefore prohibiting the appearance of a quantum field theory. Second, for the hyperfinite factors of Araki, Woods and Powers, we prove a quantitative equivalence: The limiting factor is of type III if and only if the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic diverges. This divergence is necessary to generate the continuous spectrum associated to a type III factor. Thus, in this setting, the emergence of a type III factor requires not merely the presence of magic, but an infinite amount of it. These results provide a rigorous setting supporting the proposal that infinite magic is a necessary structural ingredient for the emergence of a relativistic continuum from lattice systems.
